title: The Budd Company and also Other Stuff
premise: A commissioned Transport Fever dome-car showcase grows into a history of metallurgy, Budd and American rail procurement. The presenter and guest Miles explain material tradeoffs and Budd’s unusually durable stainless passenger cars. They argue that shrinking demand, bespoke procurement, protectionist factory churn and rigid safety rules undermined stable domestic rail manufacturing. Miles brings industrial-design and rail history to the conversation.
coverage: Dome cars, metallurgy, Budd’s railcar history and American procurement, from the opening commission through the patron credits and fare-token ending. Historical and engineering claims are the speakers’ account; some dates and locations remain uncertain.

panels.camera: Locked elevated oblique view.
panels.action: A smoky red locomotive and silver passenger consist traverse the station.

panels.heading: Mustard, but worse pacing
panels.description: A tilted screenshot of the Mustard channel overlays the simulated railway.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: Self-deprecating comparison: the polished explainer channel is literally pasted over this supposedly less polished video.

panels.heading: Commissioned dome cars
panels.description: Santa Fe-liveried engines pull silver dome cars through a stone-towered station.
panels.camera: Fixed three-quarter station view.
panels.action: Locomotives pass, followed by raised-glass dome cars.

panels.heading: Three model variants
panels.description: A silver dome coach is isolated against black, followed by a longer full-dome model.
panels.camera: Cuts between isolated model renders.
panels.action: Model display; no physical character action.

panels.heading: The passenger experience
panels.description: Archive footage looks forward over fluted car roofs toward a curving train. Presenter explains lounge seating versus Transport Fever regular seating.
panels.camera: Onboard forward-looking view of the curving train and passing landscape.
panels.action: The train advances through wooded terrain.

panels.heading: Aluminum labels questioned
panels.description: The game purchase menu displays passenger cars as the presenter disputes material descriptions; a real Golden Sands photograph follows.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.notes: The car materials are disputed by the presenter.

panels.heading: Primitive humans, cartoon version
panels.description: The Flintstones family and Dino ride their stone-age car.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: Anachronistic cartoon cutaway literalizes primitive humans and simple stone tools; it launches the playful metallurgy detour.

panels.heading: Minecraft metallurgy setup
panels.description: First-person Minecraft approaches a wooden house, then ore photographs overlay its fireplace.
panels.camera: First-person view approaches the doorway and turns into the room.
panels.action: Player moves into the house; crosshair, hand and inventory remain visible.
panels.visualGag: Setup of the recurring Minecraft house-fire sequence: a cozy wooden home becomes an increasingly disastrous background to a calm materials lecture.

panels.heading: Bronze and bloomery
panels.description: A bronze vessel and smoking earthen bloomery replace the game view. A photograph of a corroded curved iron blade briefly illustrates iron smelting.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Kingsford before its time
panels.description: A Kingsford charcoal bag is composited beside the historical bloomery.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: Modern barbecue packaging makes the ancient charcoal fuel explanation deliberately mundane and anachronistic.

panels.heading: Hammering iron, cozy fire
panels.description: Minecraft player faces the fireplace and framed tools.
panels.camera: The view shows turns between fireplace and wall.
panels.action: First-person player turns within the wooden room.
panels.visualGag: House-fire setup continues: the fireplace appears contained here, before the lecture background catches fire.

panels.heading: Slag leaves a grain
panels.description: Close-up microstructure illustrates fibers of impurities in wrought iron.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: China got there first
panels.description: Chinese illustrated furnace page interrupts the European furnace reconstruction; presenter jokes that China was not telling anyone.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Monastic industry
panels.description: Cistercian heraldic crest and waterwheel photographs illustrate the presenter’s account of monastery furnaces.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Furnace shopping list
panels.description: Ore, Kingsford charcoal, coke and a pale stone image accumulate on black.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: The modern Kingsford bag returns as a comic everyday prop in an otherwise technical historical recipe.

panels.heading: Blast furnace mechanism
panels.description: Cross-section labels hot-air blast, molten iron and slag outlets; subsequent pig-iron and finery illustrations complete the process.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Finery products
panels.description: A frying pan and blacksmith photograph are pasted over the finery engraving. A photograph of two sledgehammers follows to illustrate hand tools.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.notes: The collage illustrates cast-iron and wrought-iron products.

panels.heading: The wooden lecture room ignites
panels.description: Flames appear along the Minecraft room’s wooden wall beside the still-contained brick fireplace.
panels.camera: First-person turns between doorway, fireplace and wall.
panels.action: Fire spreads to wooden blocks; player continues looking around.
panels.visualGag: First payoff of the house-fire setup: the lecturer keeps discussing tools while the home itself begins to burn.

panels.heading: An unwelcome visitor at the burning house
panels.description: Player turns from spreading fire to the wooden door, where a Minecraft zombie’s green face and arm show through its windows.
panels.camera: First-person turn from the burning fireplace wall to the doorway.
panels.action: A zombie waits outside the door while the interior burns.
panels.visualGag: The materials lecture continues despite the burning room and zombie at the door. The later Rotten Flesh hotbar label adds another incongruous gameplay detail.
panels.notes: The zombie is outside the door. No attack or kill is shown, and the Rotten Flesh label does not explain how the item was acquired.

panels.heading: Fire escalates under metallurgy
panels.description: Ceiling and walls show larger flames; sword microstructure briefly interrupts. The selected-item caption reads Rotten Flesh while the zombie and fire complicate the scene.
panels.camera: The first-person view turns around the room.
panels.action: Burning ceiling blocks and wall gaps expand.
panels.visualGag: The unattended house fire keeps getting worse under the metallurgy lecture.
panels.notes: The selected-item caption reads Rotten Flesh; no kill or item acquisition is shown.

panels.heading: Definitions over disaster
panels.description: White steel/carbon definitions cover Minecraft as the roof burns.
panels.camera: First-person turns continue under fixed text overlays.
panels.action: Text builds from steel to cast iron to wrought iron while flames consume blocks.
panels.visualGag: Deadpan educational text competes with the collapsing wooden-house background: calm precision versus visibly worsening disaster.

panels.heading: Floating inferno payoff
panels.description: Outside, suspended burning timber and leaf blocks frame the damaged house.
panels.camera: The first-person view turns and tilts around the burning house.
panels.action: Player exits/looks around the burning exterior; blocks disappear as fire progresses.
panels.visualGag: House-fire payoff: the lecture finally reveals the scale of the ruin; Minecraft’s floating blocks amplify the absurdity.

panels.heading: Iron Bridge survives
panels.description: Red iron arch at Shropshire introduces cast-iron construction and carpentry joints.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Tay Bridge reversal
panels.description: Intact Tay Bridge photograph sets up the next photograph of collapsed spans.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: The intact bridge gives way to collapsed spans as the presenter says “It doesn’t stand today…It fell over.” The abrupt switch matches his deadpan delivery.

panels.heading: It fell over
panels.description: Collapsed Tay Bridge spans lie in the water.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: Payoff of intact-versus-ruined bridge comparison; the abrupt image substitution matches the blunt spoken answer.

panels.heading: More carbon equals…
panels.description: MORE CARBON = appears alone at the top of a black card.
panels.camera: Static graphic, followed by additional images on the same card.
panels.action: Blank space waits for the illustrated strength and ductility tradeoff.
panels.visualGag: The empty equation will acquire a strongman to represent strength and a duck to stand in for ductility.

panels.heading: More carbon, more strength
panels.description: An unidentified historical weightlifter appears below MORE CARBON = and MORE STRENGTH; the photograph’s original source is unknown.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: The weightlifter makes strength literal; a duck will appear under LESS DUCTILITY. The later buff-test bodybuilder repeats the strength joke.

panels.heading: Less duck-tility
panels.description: The MORE CARBON = card pairs a weightlifter labelled MORE STRENGTH with a duck photograph labelled LESS DUCTILITY.
panels.camera: Held two-image graphic.
panels.action: Static photo collage adds the duck as the second half of the comparison.
panels.visualGag: The duck turns the first syllable of ductility into a visual pun beside the literal image of human strength.
panels.notes: The photographs’ original sources and the weightlifter’s identity are unknown. The duck is a photograph, not a named cartoon character.

panels.heading: Unbendable Bender
panels.description: Two Bender bending robots from Futurama hold a beam marked UNBENDABLE.
panels.camera: Cut to the cartoon as the beam changes orientation.
panels.action: The two cartoon robots hold the beam; its orientation changes.
panels.visualGag: Futurama bending-robot cutaway turns ductility into an immediately recognizable cartoon joke.

panels.heading: Compression setup
panels.description: A skillet has two red arrows pointing inward.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: The cookware becomes a miniature structural diagram, beginning a sequence that will snap the skillet in two.

panels.heading: Tension reversal
panels.description: The same skillet now has red arrows pointing outward.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: The arrows reverse direction before the drawn break in the skillet.

panels.heading: Skillet snaps
panels.description: The pan is crudely split into two separated halves, red lines emphasizing the break.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: The deliberately rough split finishes the skillet sequence by drawing brittle tensile failure.

panels.heading: Real wreckage
panels.description: Archival bridge debris and damaged rolling stock replace the diagram; Iron Bridge subsequently returns as the compression counterexample.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Not like Minecraft
panels.description: Minecraft returns to the burnt house and chest of ranked materials.
panels.camera: First-person view enters the damaged house, then the inventory opens.
panels.action: Player opens a chest containing metal/diamond items.
panels.visualGag: Callback to the house-fire sequence: after the destructive game demonstration, the presenter explicitly rejects the game’s simple hierarchy of better materials.

panels.heading: Tool versus truss
panels.description: Cutting tools and a long-span truss illustrate the presenter’s tradeoff argument, followed by low/high-carbon summary and stress-strain graph.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Penn Station, now and then
panels.description: Modern Penn entrance/concourse cuts to old station exterior and crowded hall. Presenter describes the modern station as a rat’s warren.
panels.camera: Cuts between modern stills and archival views.
panels.action: Crowds/cars change in archival footage; modern photographs are static.

panels.heading: Hand of progress
panels.description: A historic cartoon labels the HAND OF PROGRESS tearing down blocks for a terminal.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: The oversized hand treats buildings like loose toy blocks. Its grand promise of progress accompanies a turn toward railroad safety.

panels.heading: Wooden cars and tunnels
panels.description: Transport Fever wooden coaches approach/exit a tunnel as narrator explains fire danger and the belief steel cars would shake apart.
panels.camera: Locked oblique trackside view.
panels.action: Steam locomotive pulls red wooden-style coaches along the tunnel approach.

panels.heading: Gibbs and Altoona
panels.description: George Gibbs plaque, Altoona shops postcard and prototype subway-car photograph illustrate the risk taken by IRT.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Steel production becomes possible
panels.description: Side elevation of Gibbs car and Pennsylvania coach photos lead to the preserved P50H museum car.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: MP54 longevity
panels.description: Historic electric commuter cars with pantographs illustrate the 1908 to 1981 service-life claim; game recreations pass between reference photos.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: A shed on wheels setup
panels.description: Side-on red Pennsylvania coach isolates the body and underframe before annotations.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: The plain coach sets up the decorated-shed joke: it will acquire an I AM A MONUMENT sign as if it were architecture.

panels.heading: Decorated shed, monument
panels.description: A red outline surrounds the coach body with a sketched rooftop billboard saying I AM A MONUMENT.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: The rooftop monument sign turns the coach into a comic illustration of the decorated shed. The same image returns during the discussion of painting costs.

panels.heading: Alloys for different jobs
panels.description: Boron/tungsten/silicon specimens, periodic table, Sputnik and a nuclear-load train appear in a quick materials montage.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.notes: The nuclear railway image is an illustration.

panels.heading: Decorated-shed callback
panels.description: The I AM A MONUMENT coach returns before Sherwin Williams’ COVER THE EARTH logo.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: Callback to the earlier architectural-shed joke; the exaggerated paint-brand image makes avoided painting costs concrete.

panels.heading: Stainless has a joining problem
panels.description: Rust around dissimilar-metal fasteners illustrates the difficulty, then Edward Budd portrait and company builder plate introduce the solution.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Miles joins
panels.description: Model caboose, simulated Golden Gate Bridge and simulated San Francisco buildings introduce industrial designer/model maker Miles and Presidio Bay.
panels.camera: Montage of model footage and game views, with changing angles around the caboose.
panels.action: Introduction illustrated by models and game scenes rather than an onscreen speaking head.

panels.heading: McKeen motor car
panels.description: Historic steel motor car with circular windows, interior and pointed-nose views illustrate the guests’ account of Budd’s early work.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Wind splitter reversal
panels.description: Plan and side drawings show the pointed and rounded ends. The guests say the visually streamlined end is not the more aerodynamic one.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.notes: The aerodynamic comparison is the guests’ claim.

panels.heading: Telescoping wooden cars
panels.description: Wrecked wooden passenger-car photograph explains the safety problem before Michelin stainless vehicles.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

sound.text: Michelin is mispronounced as part of the French-name gag.

panels.heading: French collaboration
panels.description: Citroën Traction Avant photograph, rubber-tired railcar museum display and American stainless DMU illustrate the Michelin experiment.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

sound.text: Citroën is mispronounced in the recurring French-name gag.
Traction Avant gets the same French-name mispronunciation treatment.

panels.heading: Learning to weld stainless
panels.description: Archive workers and forming machinery lead into car-shell assembly, tying failed DMUs to successful fabrication techniques.
panels.camera: Cuts among machinery close-ups, elevated assembly views and workers using tools.
panels.action: Workers operate machinery and work along a silver car shell.
panels.notes: The welding-invention attributions are the guests’ claims.

panels.heading: Pioneer Zephyr success
panels.description: Burlington Zephyr and Flying Yankee reference images follow engine/factory footage, then game streamliner passes.
panels.camera: Cuts from held reference images to fixed game trackside framing.
panels.action: Game train approaches and crosses frame; historical photos static.
panels.notes: The speech says Yankee Clipper, while the photograph is labelled FLYING YANKEE.

panels.heading: Speed, publicity, Silver Streak
panels.description: Streamliner passes the game station as guests discuss speed, fuel and the earlier Silver Streak film, not the Pryor/Wilder one.
panels.camera: Fixed trackside view.
panels.action: Silver simulated streamliner passes waiting platform figures.
panels.notes: The Silver Streak film correction is spoken; no mistaken-film poster appears.

panels.heading: One-off streamliners
panels.description: Stacked archival photographs of Rebel, Comet, Crusader and other streamlined trains illustrate the one-off era.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Separate locomotives and cars
panels.description: Archive footage shows train on a coast, station arrival, boarding and dome interior before scenic onboard footage.
panels.camera: Cuts across coast, platform and interior viewpoints; later forward onboard view changes with train travel.
panels.action: Train approaches/passes; people gather at doorways; scenery moves past dome windows.

panels.heading: Who invented the dome?
panels.description: Vista Dome advertisement shows Burlington Silver Dome under A THRILLING INNOVATION IN TRAVEL ENJOYMENT. Miles corrects the presenter’s Pullman assumption.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Back to the commission
panels.description: Transport Fever station and passing dome cars return after the historical scenic footage.
panels.camera: Fixed station view.
panels.action: Locomotives and different dome-car models pass in sequence.

panels.heading: Great Dome retired
panels.description: Times Union article announces Amtrak’s Great Dome retirement.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: The Great Dome retirement and a disappointed travel plan set up the angry FIRE Anderson insert.

panels.heading: FIRE Anderson
panels.description: A derelict industrial building bears an edited red/blue FIRE / Anderson ! sign.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: The edited sign turns one speaker’s insult at Amtrak leadership into a literal firing demand.
panels.notes: It is unclear which speaker delivers the Dick Anderson insult.

panels.heading: Big domes to high-levels
panels.description: Santa Fe full-dome passenger photograph leads into archive maintenance and old doodlebug image as RDC discussion begins.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: The RDC drive train
panels.description: Archive low underbody view shows a car moving away over the camera, followed by forward railway view and driver footage.
panels.camera: Low fixed inspection-pit viewpoint; cuts to forward traveling view and driver close-up.
panels.action: Car underside passes overhead and recedes; driver handles cab controls.

panels.heading: RDCs still working
panels.description: WES photograph and Canadian-flagged RDC image illustrate surviving equipment. Guest is unsure which Canadian province.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.notes: The guest remains unsure of the Canadian province.

panels.heading: Patent advantage
panels.description: Repeated archive fluting/forming/welding sequence accompanies the distinction between full stainless structure and bolted-on sheathing.
panels.camera: Machine/worker montage; changing worker positions.
panels.action: Workers handle tools against a car shell.

panels.heading: Durability sent underwater
panels.description: An excavator tips a subway car over a barge edge.
panels.camera: Cut to the barge.
panels.action: The subway car hangs tipped over the water’s edge.
panels.visualGag: A long-lived stainless passenger car is deliberately sent into the sea, then reappears as a fish habitat.

panels.heading: Fish in the subway
panels.description: Fish swims inside submerged railcar framing.
panels.camera: Held underwater view.
panels.action: A fish swims near the submerged supports.
panels.visualGag: The railcar sent over the barge now houses fish. Its corrosion-resistant passenger space has become an aquatic habitat.

panels.heading: Washboard comparison
panels.description: Historic New Haven silver-sided electric car follows the reef view, illustrating presenter’s question about sheathing and rust.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Patreon for a private train
panels.description: Game dome cars pass beneath a high fixed viewpoint as the two speakers joke about private-car buying and Patreon funding.
panels.camera: Fixed elevated railway framing.
panels.action: Silver passenger train passes and recedes.
panels.notes: The private-train and 80-years-to-leak jokes are spoken over ordinary train imagery.

panels.heading: Presidio Bay invitation
panels.description: An unfinished city build, Bay Area archive photos and concept sketches accompany the guest’s plug. One still shows a white statue head-first on pavement beneath stone arches; its identity and why it is there are unknown.
panels.camera: Montage of simulated aerial views, photos, books and drawn concepts.
panels.action: Game views change position; historical photographs and plans static.

panels.heading: What happened to Budd?
panels.description: Game mainline scene returns as presenter turns from guest farewell to passenger-rail market decline.
panels.camera: Fixed elevated view along multiple tracks.
panels.action: Train emerges from distance and passes below viewpoint.

panels.heading: Highways, airlines, mail, speed rules
panels.description: Highway aerial, Pan American jet, railway post-office car and T-79/P-70/F-60 track sign illustrate presenter’s competing explanations.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Lightweight Keystone
panels.description: Green-and-white Budd illustration of low-slung Pennsylvania car accompanies tubular construction and claimed 60% weight reduction.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Metroliner experiment
panels.description: Pennsylvania Metroliner photograph cuts to game electric trains passing one another; presenter says fast tests blew neighboring MP54 windows.
panels.camera: Fixed game station viewpoint.
panels.action: Red commuter and silver modern electric consists pass on neighboring tracks.
panels.notes: The window damage is narrated, not shown in the game.

panels.heading: Jets on an RDC
panels.description: M-497 nose, PRIDE OF THE CENTRAL plate and rooftop jet nacelles appear before a B-36 photograph.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.notes: The jet-powered railcar was a real experiment.

panels.heading: Speed record correction
panels.description: Archive jet-powered railcar approaches amid dust with *183 MPH overlay.
panels.camera: Fixed trackside view of the approaching car, its pass and the dust cloud left behind.
panels.action: Jet railcar rushes past camera, leaving dust.
panels.visualGag: The *183 MPH overlay corrects the spoken 178 mph figure while the jet-powered railcar rushes past.
panels.notes: The onscreen 183 MPH corrects the spoken 178 MPH.

panels.heading: Transit keeps production alive
panels.description: Budd Metropolitan/Pioneer III brochures, PATCO and CTA photographs illustrate the commuter/subway orders.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Amfleet to TransitAmerica
panels.description: Amfleet II passenger-features advertisement and TransitAmerica image lead into factory interior and replacement golf-course aerial.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Factory becomes golf course
panels.description: Green golf-course tract amid industrial buildings replaces the factory photograph, followed by ThyssenKrupp Budd gate.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.notes: The presenter identifies the site and corporate sequence.

panels.heading: They were too good
panels.description: THEY WERE TOO GOOD! appears across the passing simulated train.
panels.camera: Fixed station view.
panels.visualGag: THEY WERE TOO GOOD! celebrates the durability that, in the presenter’s account, left the company struggling for replacement orders.

panels.heading: Cars outlive their builder
panels.description: Budd R32 subway photograph follows VIA and Amtrak images, illustrating long service lives before the disruptive-technology/early-retirement conclusion.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Buy America requirements
panels.description: Federal Transit Administration webpage overlays the game train, setting up the new procurement mechanism.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Step one: write bespoke specs
panels.description: STEP 1 request-for-bids title shares frame with SEPTA Silverliner V technical specification cover.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Step two: build the whole apparatus
panels.description: STEP 2 foreign manufacturers develop bids involving a US-based factory, tooling and hiring.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Step three: low bid

panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Crony capitalism correction

panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: Adding IS JUST CAPITALISM turns the apparent criticism of crony capitalism into a criticism of capitalism itself.

panels.heading: Step five: lay workers off

panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Step six: close the factory

panels.heading: Budd licenses abroad
panels.description: TOKYU builder plates visibly identify manufacture under license from THE BUDD COMPANY; Japanese EMUs and bogie photographs follow.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: Australia and Brazil
panels.description: Comeng stainless car/LIRR bilevel, Mafersa logo, São Paulo Metro and VRE cars illustrate international descendants of Budd designs.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.

panels.heading: American everything setup
panels.description: US flag starts small on black and grows while narrator lists American design, workers, materials, location and government funding.
panels.camera: A US flag graphic grows within the fixed black frame.
panels.visualGag: Each American input makes the patriotic flag larger until it fills the screen, ready for the overseas-profits reversal.

panels.heading: Profits overseas payoff
panels.description: EU flag replaces the US flag during overseas-profits/protectionism conclusion.
panels.camera: Cut to a still photograph or graphic.
panels.visualGag: The EU flag replaces the growing US flag when the profits go overseas. “It works, folks” delivers the sarcastic verdict on protectionism.

panels.heading: Budd never really died
panels.description: Game station/dome trains return as narrator says Budd was offshored and made needlessly expensive.
panels.camera: Fixed elevated station framing.
panels.action: Locomotive and dome consist pass platform.

panels.heading: Commercial, not Franklin
panels.description: Same station model accompanies renewed Franklin promise, Patreon/Killdozer support invitation and joke that viewers could pirate it.
panels.camera: Held game station view.
panels.notes: The Prager insult is spoken over the game station.

panels.heading: Ad-free disasters podcast plug
panels.description: Game station remains visible through ad-free rationale, Alice Avizandum engineering-disasters project and Twitter plug.
panels.camera: Fixed station framing.
panels.action: Another simulated train approaches and passes.

panels.heading: Patron credits
panels.description: MY PATRONS heading begins the dense white-on-black scrolling roll.
panels.camera: Fixed view of upward-scrolling credits.

sound.text: Brahms’s Tragic Overture, Op. 81, performed by the Musopen Symphony, is credited for the patron roll.

panels.notes: The video credits Brahms’s Tragic Overture, Op. 81, performed by the Musopen Symphony.

panels.heading: One fare end token
panels.description: GOOD FOR ONE FARE / DNE transit token occupies black background after the patron names.
panels.camera: Held end-card framing, followed by black.
panels.action: Token end card remains, then disappears into black.
